slides.title: Things your doctor wishes you'd just ask

slides.q: Is it normal for my heart to race after coffee?
slides.a: Caffeine is a stimulant, so a faster heartbeat or jittery feeling is a common reaction, and some people are much more sensitive than others. Try a smaller cup, or have it with food. Worth seeing a doctor if it comes with chest pain, fainting, shortness of breath, or your heart races even without caffeine.

slides.q: Why do I have a sore throat every morning?
slides.a: Often it's dry air or breathing through your mouth while you sleep, which dries out your throat overnight. Allergies, post-nasal drip, and acid reflux can also cause it. A humidifier and staying hydrated help. Worth seeing a doctor if it lasts more than a couple of weeks, comes with fever, or you snore heavily.

slides.q: Why does my skin itch after a hot shower?
slides.a: Hot water strips away your skin's natural oils, leaving it dry and itchy, especially in winter. Try lukewarm water, shorter showers, and moisturizer on damp skin right after. Fragrance-free products help too. Worth seeing a doctor if the itch is intense, comes with a rash or hives, or doesn't improve with these changes.

slides.q: Why do I get a bump in my armpit after shaving?
slides.a: Usually it's an ingrown hair or an irritated hair follicle, and it tends to settle down on its own within a week or two. Warm compresses help, and so does shaving with the grain using a sharp blade. Don't squeeze it. Worth seeing a doctor if a lump lasts more than two weeks, keeps growing, or feels hard.

slides.q: Why do my gums bleed when I floss?
slides.a: Usually it's early gum inflammation from plaque building up along the gumline. It sounds backwards, but flossing gently every day is usually the fix, and bleeding often eases within a week or two. Brush softly with a soft brush. Worth seeing a dentist if it keeps happening, your gums are swollen, or they're pulling back.
